title: Dark matter self-interactions and small-scale structure
bottleneck: Cold dark matter simulations predict dense cusps and abundant satellite galaxies that observations of dwarf galaxies do not show, the core-cusp and too-big-to-fail problems. Self-interacting dark matter can fix the discrepancies but requires a cross section tuned to a narrow window, while baryonic feedback explanations remain disputed.
why_it_blocks: If dark matter is not perfectly collisionless, its particle properties can be read off from galactic structure; if the discrepancies are just astrophysics, a major discovery channel evaporates.
current_state: Precision stellar kinematics from Gaia and strong-lensing measurements are sharpening the small-scale tests, but no consensus has emerged between self-interactions and feedback solutions. Strong gravitational lensing of quasars and stellar streams in the Milky Way halo provide independent small-scale tests that are sharpening rapidly.
